text:
anya: seeing a stair-step tail p99 spike from the adaptive batcher in us-west-2 starting ~10:30 UTC. p99 180ms -> 920ms, throughput down ~35%. anyone on this? :eyes:
simon: yep, canary shows same. continuous-batcher logs have microbatch sizes oscillating 1 -> 8 -> 2 every ~10s. kernel-selector is flipping between fused_v2 and fallback on alternating batches. attaching a quick trace below.
rachel: trace snippet:
```
# continuous-batcher: batch_id=7123 size=1 kernel=fallback latency=820ms kv_hit=false
# kernel-selector: decision=fallback reason=small_microbatch
# kv-cache: evict key=kv://user:abc cause=memory_pressure
# admission: qlen=18 throttle=0.6
```
kevin: didn't we change the qbatch heuristic in commit 4d2f0b7 last night? @simon can you pull kernel-selector metrics and recent commits. sounds like a mispick under jitter.
simon: metrics dump: "kernel_choice: fused_v2=40%, fallback=60% (oscillating), microbatch_target=4, actual_sizes=[1,8,2,1,6,1,7]"
priya: hypothesis: admission control sees transient qlen spikes, raises throttle, continuous-batcher fragments requests into tiny microbatches. tiny microbatches force the selector to pick fallback (higher per-batch overhead) -> visible stutter. KV cache sees churn (evictions ~10/s) which increases latency for fallback batches. not a single noisy tenant.
anya: confirmed — tenant traces look flat. spikes align with kernel flips + kv-evict bursts.
kevin: two quick mitigations: 1) revert the selector change, or 2) increase min_microbatch_size floor (hot-reload). which is faster to test on canary?
simon: changing min_microbatch_size is lighter and hot-reloadable. i'll push min_microbatch_size=4 to canary now.
deploy-bot: deploy started: update config min_microbatch_size=4 -> canary (id: dpl-7891) :rocket:
simon: canary 5m after: p99 down to ~240ms, throughput +28%. kernel flips reduced: fused_v2=92% now.
rachel: KV evictions dropped 10/s -> 1/s after canary. KV hit rate up from 71% -> 93%. profile shows fewer fallback kernel handoffs.
anya: nice. keep the config as a temporary mitigation and schedule selector stability work. please open a PR to add a safety floor and smoothing to the kernel selector.
priya: filed issue #3321 with traces, metrics and suggested selector-windowing fix.
simon: rolling the canary config to prod now.
deploy-bot: deploy success: dpl-7891 -> prod (completed). Health checks: all green.
kevin: quick summary for postmortem: root cause = kernel-selector too sensitive to microbatch size + admission-control oscillation leading to microbatch fragmentation and KV-cache thrash. mitigation = increase min_microbatch_size floor + revert/patch selector. next steps: add selector smoothing, improve admission backpressure policy, add alert on microbatch oscillation.
anya: closing the thread for now. please ping me if it reappears and add the incident notes to the perf-incidents doc. :thumbsup:
